title: Avocado and banana mash
summary: A no-cook, two-ingredient first food: creamy, mild and ready in five minutes.
texture: Very smooth, like thick yogurt, with no lumps for first tastes. Thin with a little breast milk or formula if it's too thick. Once baby handles it easily, leave it slightly thicker.
ingredients: 1/4 small ripe banana (brown spots are good)
1 to 2 tsp breast milk or prepared infant formula, to thin (optional)
steps: Wash your hands. Scoop the avocado flesh into a small bowl.
Add the banana and mash both with a fork until completely smooth. For an extra-smooth first taste, press it through a fine sieve or use a small blender.
Stir in breast milk or formula a little at a time until it drops easily off a spoon.
Offer a few small spoonfuls. Let baby lean in for the spoon, and stop when they turn away.
choking: Mash until there are no firm pieces of avocado left; under-ripe avocado stays in hard chunks, so only use one that dents when you press it.
Serve on a spoon or as a thin smear on a pre-loaded spoon, not as cubes, at this stage.
storage: Best made fresh: avocado and banana turn brown fast. Cover the leftover with plastic wrap pressed onto the surface and use within a few hours (fridge). Don't freeze.
tips: Brown spots on the banana mean it's sweeter and softer, so it mashes smoother.
Want to serve it baby-led? Offer a ripe avocado spear about the length of an adult finger instead, rolled in a little baby oat cereal for grip.
